name: Keisei-Takasago
tagline: Tokyo in 35 minutes and Otemachi in 37 minutes. Served by 5 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Katsushika City, where Keisei and Hokuso Railway run 5 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 37 minutes to Otemachi, 50 minutes to Shinjuku, 56 minutes to Shibuya and 47 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.8 m to 1.6 m, a difference of 0.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 7 clinics and 5 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is かつしか江戸川病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 5 lines serve the station. Keisei Main Line and Keisei Oshiage Line run through it. Keisei Kanamachi Line also call here. Narita Sky Access Line and Hokuso Line are available too. The lines are split between operators (Keisei runs 4 lines and Hokuso Railway runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Keisei Oshiage Line runs at 157% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 京成曳舟→押上; trains from here toward 押上 pass through it. Keisei Main Line runs at 137% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大神宮下→京成船橋, which this station is not on. Hokuso Line runs at 90% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 新柴又→京成高砂, which includes this station. Keisei Kanamachi Line and Narita Sky Access Line is not covered by the ministry's congestion survey. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 2LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. 5 lines and a wide choice of connections and schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, a large projected flood depth holds it down.

neighbours.lead: For the number of medical facilities, Shibamata; for how close the centre is, Keisei-Takasago.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Keisei-Takasago. Both have the Keisei Kanamachi Line. Keisei-Takasago also has the 4 lines, which Shibamata does not. Keisei-Takasago is at least 7 minutes quicker to Roppongi and Toranomon. On quiet, though, Shibamata comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For the number of medical facilities, Aoto; for what it offers families, Keisei-Takasago.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Keisei-Takasago in a straight line. Both have the Keisei Main Line, Keisei Oshiage Line and Narita Sky Access Line. Keisei-Takasago also has the Keisei Kanamachi Line and Hokuso Line, which Aoto does not. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. On the number of medical facilities, Aoto comes out ahead. Within about 13 minutes' walk, Aoto has 34 clinics and pharmacies and Keisei-Takasago has 13.

goodFor: People who want another route when a line stops
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People living alone who want to hold the rent down
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: 王子金町市川線 (1 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 6 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 5 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning trains are very crowded: Keisei Oshiage Line trains toward 押上 pass through the line's busiest stretch further on.
